sharedChannel.note: `args.deps` is ONE dependency channel that every heavy stage reads, and bindAttempt interpolates it into each of their prompts. The COUNT of those stages has been wrong twice in prose -- it said nine and meant ten, then finish became an eleventh the day it was bound -- so the suite stopped typing a number and derives the set from canonical bytes instead.
sharedChannel.literalWhy: every consumer hands the shared list to bindAttempt in this exact form, so counting the non-comment lines that carry it counts the consumers. A refactor that changes the spelling drops the derived count to zero rather than quietly to ten, and either way it stops matching the set this suite renders and fails loudly.
sharedChannel.fedChannelWhy: exactly one non-comment line carries the literal WITHOUT being a consumer: the grade's fallback, `args.gradeDeps == null ? (args.deps || []) : args.gradeDeps`. That line is the channel being FED -- a grade is what the dedicated channel exists to divert off the shared one -- not a twelfth stage reading it. The test asserts that line still exists BEFORE subtracting it, so the exclusion can never quietly hide a real consumer.
sharedChannel.consumersWhy: this roster is NOT what the test counts -- canonical bytes are. It is here so a failure can NAME the stage nobody rendered, and it is asserted to be the same size as the derived set, so a stage added to one and not the other fails instead of drifting. `finish` joined when it was rebound through bindAttempt; `fix-ac` had been a consumer all along while going unnamed in the prose that enumerated them.

finish.note: FINISH was an UNBOUND dispatch until it was rebound through bindAttempt: it was told to write its verdict into finisher/progress.md, the one file the protocol says may never carry a terminal one. Binding it moved its terminal onto the reserved write-once finisher/cleanup-report-{n}.md and made it the ELEVENTH consumer of the shared args.deps channel.
finish.notUnderT0: its prompt cannot join the seven-builder attribution freeze, for a reason adjacent to the measurement lane's but not the same: not that the stage is younger than t0, but that the BINDING is. The t0 snapshot carries this dispatch with no reserved attempt and no carrier at all, so a t0-vs-today hunk comparison would report the entire carrier as undeclared drift while proving nothing about the prompt. Re-pointing t0 is not the fix -- section 20's notEqual guard exists to stop exactly that.
finish.insteadPinned: the prompt BODY is frozen by declared digest, exactly as measure.bornAfterT0 freezes its three. Worth the same and no more: it stops ACCIDENTAL drift outright and makes deliberate drift a RECORDED act, and it does not stop a hand that re-pins the digest instead of writing a `changes` entry.
finish.digestOf: the body the dispatch AUTHORS, captured at the bindAttempt seam before the carrier goes on. Digesting the BOUND form would freeze the carrier a second time (the seven-builder attribution already covers it) and, worse here than anywhere else, would make this pin move with the dependency channel -- which is the one thing this stage is separately measured for.
finish.reservedTerminalWhy: the rendered region MINTS this path from canonical bytes -- `seed('finish') + 1` with artifact `cleanup-report` -- so it is not a value this suite types. It is the exact write-once record a cache-missing replay re-mints onto (execution-evidence section 1 A4): a relaunch that bumps only attempts.grade leaves attempts.finish unbumped, and a finish prompt re-rendered through the shared channel then replays onto bytes already consumed.
finish.t0OrderWhy: the finish prompt must never name progress.md in the same breath as the STATUS ask: that ORDERS the verdict into the one file that may not hold one (closeSweep.progressRule), and it is what this dispatch really said until it was bound. The close sweep catches the shape generically across every prompt; this asserts it stayed fixed at the site that actually had it, and that the t0 order it was fixed away from is still quotable.

closeSweep.note: The close-the-artifact obligation checked in the STAGE PROMPTS the run dispatches -- roleFiles above checks the other side, the role files those prompts are handed to. The site set is DERIVED FROM THE CANONICAL FILE at runtime (a string-aware walk finds every prompt that asks for a STATUS line) and is deliberately NOT listed here. A list of line numbers is precisely the defect this effort shipped twice: the seventh prompt added tomorrow is the prompt nobody checks. What IS data here is the ASK vocabulary, the credited MECHANISMS and the EXCLUSION set -- each a judgement a reviewer must be able to argue with.
closeSweep.limit: The sweep reads SOURCE bytes and sees a prompt only if it asks in one of the phrasings below. A prompt assembled at runtime out of strings this file does not contain, or one that asks for its verdict in words nobody has written yet, is invisible to it. It also says NOTHING about compliance: it measures what the prompt REQUESTS, never what an agent does.
closeSweep.clauseFrom: roleFiles.requiredClause -- the SAME three phrases, not a second copy. The obligation is one sentence whether a role file states it or a prompt interpolates it, and two wordings would be two obligations.

asks.why: the long spelling. Matched as a literal, never as a regex over English: a detector that guesses at phrasing is how a sweep quietly stops describing the file it guards.

the short spelling, and a prefix of the decorated forms (`END with STATUS: BLOCKED`, `END with STATUS (CLEAN = ...`), so those need no row of their own. Two asks inside one prompt collapse to one site by span.

asks.phrase: END your reply with that same STATUS line
asks.why: the grade's own spelling. GRADE_PROMPT states the close obligation inline and then asks for the line in the REPLY, so neither short form appears in it. Without this row the one prompt that states the clause twice would be the one prompt the sweep never sees.

mechanisms.why: the BOUND carrier. bindAttempt states closeTerminal for every stage it binds and names the terminal that was reserved for it, so a prompt whose ask sits inside a bindAttempt call already carries the obligation exactly once. Restating it per stage is the duplication that produced 25 dialects of one sentence in the role files.

the UNBOUND twin: one const, interpolated by each stage that does not route through bindAttempt, taking the path it closes. A site that hand-types the sentence instead is NOT credited, and that is deliberate -- the next dialect starts with the first hand-typed copy.

closeSweep.minWhy: a floor, not an inventory. It fails the suite if the walk ever stops finding the prompts it guards -- a sweep that silently narrows to zero sites passes forever otherwise. Raising it as prompts are added is fine.

exclusions.why: propose writes a unified diff the apply stage feeds to git, not a prose record. A trailing STATUS line corrupts the patch, so the close obligation cannot attach to this artifact at all: the verdict rides in the reply, and a lost reply is reconstructed from the diff by the auditEmpty pass. The residual is REAL and this exclusion does not close it -- a propose attempt whose reply is gone has no durable verdict of its own. Closing it means minting a companion prose record for the stage to close, which is a new reserved path stage-templates.js may not mint on its own.

progressRule.sentenceSplitWhy: sentences split on a period followed by whitespace, and on newlines -- NEVER on a semicolon. `Write <session>finisher/progress.md; END with STATUS.` is ONE order, and the semicolon is exactly where a splitter would lose it.
progressRule.why: progress.md is the one file the protocol says MAY NOT carry a terminal verdict (the Producer row in section 2, and section 3). A prompt naming it in the same breath as the STATUS ask ORDERS the violation, which is what the finisher dispatch did until it was bound. bindAttempt's own step 1 names progress.md and says NEVER a terminal verdict: naming the file is correct, ordering the verdict into it is not, and only a sentence-level rule tells those two apart.

canonReach.note: HOW FAR THE SITE EXHAUSTIVENESS REACHES. The assertion over `sites` compares the FIXTURE to the RUNNERS and to nothing else. Both are written by the same hand in the same edit, so a stop the canonical file returns that NEITHER knows about is invisible to it -- which is exactly how the measurement lane shipped three stop sites with no row. canonReach.reaches: every LITERAL gate('<stage>') call site in stage-templates.js. Each one can return a route-tagged stop, so each must be covered by a declared site row above or named in gateStagesNotDeclared with a reason.
canonReach.minGateSitesWhy: a floor, not a count. It fails the suite if the sweep's pattern ever stops matching the file it guards -- a scan that silently narrows to zero passes forever otherwise.
canonReach.cannotReach: the explicit `return { stage: ... }` stops -- research, propose, review, finalize, validate, finalize-after-ac, measure, preflight, calibrate, and every transport-class return. Their stage names ARE harvestable as string literals, but a harvested name proves nothing about REACHING that stop: driving one needs a scenario and a runner per site, which is what `sites` is. The `d5: no untagged stop line survives` sweep is the only other reach into canonical bytes, and it checks TAGGING, never coverage -- a stop added there carrying a route tag and no site row passes everything in this file.
canonReach.variableStageWhy: phaseGate forwards to gate() with a stage its CALLER picks, so no literal sweep can enumerate the stages an AUTHORED script gates on. The template itself never calls phaseGate, so today that hole is empty; the assertion keeps the disclosure honest by failing if the forwarding line ever leaves the file.

bornAfterT0.note: COMPOSE / MEASURE / DISPOSITION are prompt builders BORN AFTER the carrier's t0 commit, so section 20's attribution freeze cannot hold them. Widening CARRIER_BUILDERS to include them is not merely unwise, it is INCOHERENT: attribution compares a t0 render against today's render, and there is no t0 render of a builder that did not exist at t0. Re-pointing t0 at a commit that DOES carry them is not the fix either -- section 20's notEqual guard exists to stop exactly that, and it would make the other seven builders' freeze vacuous in order to buy these three a weaker one.
bornAfterT0.instead: the three are frozen by DECLARED DIGEST. The test drives the lane, captures each prompt body at the bindAttempt seam and compares its sha256 to the pin below. Any edit to those bytes -- named by a detector or not -- fails the suite until it is declared here.
bornAfterT0.worth: HONESTLY LESS THAN THE t0 FREEZE, and the difference is the anchor. t0 is a commit no edit from this working tree can rewrite; this baseline sits in the very fixture whoever edits a prompt already owns. So it stops ACCIDENTAL drift outright and makes deliberate drift a RECORDED act -- it does not stop a hand that re-pins the digest instead of writing a `changes` entry. That is the same residual as re-pointing t0, and it is stated rather than papered over.
bornAfterT0.whyNotDetectorsAlone: the detector lists in this block (verdictDemands / statusRule / measureRequires / composeDelta / dispositionEvidence) bind the phrases they NAME and nothing else. Every byte between those phrases was unprotected: a prompt could be rewritten around them and every list would still pass. The digest is what covers the unnamed bytes; the lists are what say WHY particular bytes matter. Neither replaces the other.
bornAfterT0.digestOf: the prompt body THE LANE AUTHORS, captured before bindAttempt binds the carrier onto it. Deliberately not the bound form: the carrier's contribution to these three is already frozen by the seven-builder attribution, because it is the SAME bindAttempt helper rendering there (carrier.declaredChanges DC-1 is what a carrier edit looks like when it lands). Digesting the bound prompt would freeze the carrier twice and move all three pins on every carrier edit.

renderedFrom.why: the three values are the RESERVED TASK IDs the lane mints, which is how each prompt is picked out of the bind log rather than by position. The measure prompt is rendered once per journey, so the pinned one is this scenario's `checkout` row on its initial dispatch.

bornAfterT0.buildersPinnedAt: 2026-09-12, the bytes stage-templates.js carries in the working tree at the moment this pin was written. `bytes` is redundant to the hash and kept anyway: it is what makes the failure message legible (a prompt that grew by 400 bytes reads differently from one where a word changed).
bornAfterT0.livenessMutantWhy: proves the pin BITES on a real prompt-byte edit without writing stage-templates.js: this mutant rewrites one clause of the measure prompt in memory, so the measure digest must move and the other two must not. It is reused rather than invented because a mutant written to serve a pin can be written to serve it vacuously; this one already had to discriminate for the status-rule probe.
bornAfterT0.changesSchema: one entry per declared edit: `id`, `landed`, `reason`, `builder` (one of the three) and `marker` -- bytes the NEW render carries. The marker is asserted present in that builder's render, so an entry describing text that no longer ships fails the suite: a standing permit is not the record of one. Empty is the correct state until a prompt is deliberately edited. Re-pinning a digest without adding an entry is precisely the move this list exists to make visible.
bornAfterT0.notMeasured: NOTHING here observes an agent reading these prompts. A frozen prompt is a frozen REQUEST; whether a measurer honours it is unmeasurable in this file and closes in a live run only.

C1.title: corrected-attempt
C1.designStatement: Fail attempt 1, correct input, pass attempt 2; both evidence sets retained. Rehashing old PASS onto changed contract must fail review.
C1.historicalCitation: Synthetic; Schema QR-I1 and Backlog frozen grading
C1.coveredMechanically: that attempt 2 mints a DIFFERENT immutable path (attempt 1's record is not reachable for overwrite), that a second identity on a reserved path is refused, and that the corrected attempt's bound prompt differs from attempt 1's so it cannot replay the prior verdict from cache.
C1.notCoveredMechanically: whether attempt 1's record was actually RETAINED on disk, and whether a re-hashed old PASS was actually rejected by a review. Both are on-disk/human facts outside a pure helper. Verdict owner: T-3-spec independent review over the real attempt directories.

C2.title: false-support
C2.designStatement: Raw available:false, claimed true, no normalization -> reject. Explicit raw->normalized transform with retained lineage -> review on its actual semantics, not hashes alone.
C2.why: support is a SEMANTIC relation between an observation and a claim. No helper in stage-templates.js decides it, and no assertion in this suite can. What the suite can check -- lineage completeness -- is explicitly NOT support.

control.normalizationRule: the probe's `available` field is the claim's truth value verbatim; a skipped probe is not an availability observation
control.expectedReviewVerdict: reject -- the retained raw bytes REFUTE the claim; the lineage is complete and that is exactly why the rejection is visible

defect.expectedReviewVerdict: reject -- a normalized true with no retained raw and no stated rule is an unsupported assertion; hashing it does not make it an observation

correctedControl.claim: the probe ran and reported the capability unavailable
correctedControl.expectedReviewVerdict: accept the narrower claim only -- and note that `reason: probe skipped` means even `unavailable` is a LIMIT, not a measurement

C2.mechanicalSubcheckOnly: the suite asserts each packet's lineage fields are present/absent as declared. Passing that check is NOT evidence the claim is supported.

C3.title: unknown-return
C3.designStatement: Empty/null result with existing artifact, then missing artifact/unknown effect; reconstruction separate, no automatic repeat. Explicit observed transport + reversible/unpaid permit allows only the bounded retry; user-skip permit rejects.
C3.historicalCitation: Synthetic negative/control; Native Run unknown-output repair
C3.notCoveredMechanically: the helper cannot read journal.jsonl (rule 7), so nothing here verifies that a permit's evidencePath actually points at a real reconciliation. The suite verifies the SHAPE the permit must have; whether the orchestrator really reconciled is the reviewer's and the human's.

C4.title: changing-support
C4.designStatement: Supported -> refuted -> conflicted -> supported: completed effect receipt unchanged, affected new work/grade held, unrelated task remains eligible; restored support requires fresh grade.
C4.historicalCitation: Synthetic four-state control; Schema verifier CLI sequence
C4.why: applicability lives in references/execution-premises.md as prose obligations on the orchestrator and consumers. There is no helper in stage-templates.js that computes it, so any function this suite wrote to 'check' it would be a re-implementation grading itself.

states.completedEffectReceipt: unchanged -- the effect happened and stays history

states.affectedGrade: STALE until re-graded -- restoration does not un-stale a grade

defectVariants.inverts: the completed effect's receipt is withdrawn when the premise is refuted
defectVariants.expectedReviewVerdict: reject -- a completed effect remains history even when its premise becomes unusable

defectVariants.inverts: an UNRELATED task is held because some premise elsewhere flipped
defectVariants.expectedReviewVerdict: reject -- unrelated eligibility is distinct from affected eligibility

defectVariants.inverts: restored support silently revives the stale grade instead of requiring a fresh one
defectVariants.expectedReviewVerdict: reject -- restored support requires a fresh affected grade

C5.title: weakening-and-restoration
C5.designStatement: Remove a consumer/premise during claimed editorial revision -> reject that classification. Restoration has independent authority; unknown completed effect is reconciled first.
C5.why: 'editorial vs material' is a classification a human or an independent reviewer makes against approval.md. No helper decides it.

defect.delta: drops one declared consumer of premise P-1 and removes the premise's falsifiability clause
defect.expectedReviewVerdict: reject the CLASSIFICATION -- a weakening is material whatever it is labelled

control.delta: rewords the premise statement; the consumer list and falsifiability clause are byte-identical
control.expectedReviewVerdict: accept as editorial -- recorded, reconciled and re-reviewed without a user decision

restoration.expectedReviewVerdict: reconcile the unknown completed effect FIRST; the restoration needs its own authority and does not inherit the original authorization

C6.title: projection-defect
C6.designStatement: Fixture omits one grade dependency or assigns semantic grade to verifier -> independent AlignmentVerdict missing/invented failure; corrected fixture passes the same obligation matrix.
C6.historicalCitation: Synthetic; Native projection repair and Backlog first grade failure

every projection stage id is a plan task id
a plan task typed HITL is EXCLUDED from the projection and lands on the human checklist
each stage's agent_type equals the plan task's agent_type
the set of 64-hex hashes recoverable from the stage's CANONICALLY BOUND prompt equals the set of result hashes of its plan blockedBy edges
a blocking SEMANTIC AC maps to a stage that is (a) a different stage id from every deterministic AC's stage and (b) NOT agent_type team-verifier
files_owned of stages dispatched in the same batch are disjoint under the canonical disjoint() check

C7.title: budget-resume
C7.designStatement: Seed consumed review/verify/validate rounds and global fix dispatches, resume without reset; cap exhausts on next forbidden dispatch. Distinct test/runtime repairs charge dispatches, not fabricated extra review rounds.
C7.notCoveredMechanically: RESUME itself. Whether a resumeFromRunId relaunch replays completed agent() calls from cache -- and therefore whether seeding this segment's own replayed rounds would double-charge -- is a live runtime property. It is DERIVED from the documented contract in stage-templates.js and is NOT observed here. The suite exercises the seeding arithmetic only.

C8.title: stale-instructions
C8.designStatement: Declare changed candidate instruction hash but supply old consumed snapshot -> adoption rejected. Current source, explicit read record and consistent bounded output -> documentary acceptance only.
C8.coveredMechanically: byte comparison between a declared consumed-snapshot hash and the hash of the real source file observed at test time.
C8.notCoveredMechanically: 'documentary acceptance only' -- that a hash match licenses nothing beyond 'these are the bytes'. That boundary is a claim about what a reviewer may conclude, not a computation.
